1. Present claim petition has been filed under Section 166/140 of M.V. Act seeking compensation in respect of injuries caused to petitioner/injured Deepak Sharma in a road side accident dated 30.09.2017.

As per claim petition on 30.09.2017 MACT No.674/2017 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 1 MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:18:04 +0530 at about 2.00 p.m. petitioner along with Durgesh Rathore was going on a motorcycle which was being driven by Durgesh Rathore and petitioner was sitting as a pillion rider.

When they reached near Mahindra Showroom, Sector-2,
Noida, offending vehicle bearing registration no.DL-4CAQ-9727 being driven at a very high speed and rashly and negligently came and hit the motorcycle of the petitioner due to which both the occupants of motorcycle fell down and received serious injuries.
Both the injured were removed to Metro Hospital, Noida and petitioner was discharged on 09.10.2017.
It is stated that petitioner again admitted in said hospital on 12.10.2017 and discharged on 20.10.2017.

1 question an FIR No.1132/2017 u/s 279,338,427/506 IPC was registered at PS Sector-20, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P.
2.
It is stated that offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 at the time of accident, it was owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.
It is stated that due to accident petitioner suffered fracture on his both left side ribs, spleen injuries, fracture of left tibia and two fractures on left leg.
It is stated that at the time of accident petitioner was doing a private job and earning Rs.16,000/- per month.
3. WS to claim petition has been filed by respondent no.1 and 2 taking an objection that petitioner has suppressed material facts and respondents have been unnecessarily implicated in this case.

It is stated that vehicle of respondents was duly insured with respondent no.3 under policy no.
015745044600 valid from 01.09.2017 to 31.08.2018.

It is pleaded that on 30.09.2017 respondent no.1 was driving the MACT No.674/2017 by SHAILENDER Page 2 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:18:12 +0530 offending car and was coming from Delhi to Noida.

At the crossing near Mahindra Showroom, Sector-2, Noida, a motorbike bearing no.UP-16BN-0572 being driven by one Durgesh Rathor negligently and rashly came at very high speed, lost its balance and slipped due to over speed, driver of the bike somersaulted over the car of the respondent no.2.
Contents of claim petition have been denied.
4. In its written statement respondent no.3/insurance company has taken the objection that concerned PS has failed to forward documents to insurance company within 30 days from date of accident.
Respondent no.3 has taken all the defences in terms of Section 134(c), 147, 149, 157 and 170 of M.V. Act.
However it is admitted that offending vehicle is insured with it.
Factum of accident has been denied by insurance company.
Contents of claim petition have been denied in totality.

5. On the basis of pleadings as come on the record following issues were framed on 28.03.2018 :
(1)Whether the respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle bearing registration no.DL-4CAQ-9727 in rash and negligent manner on 30.09.2017 at 2 pm near Mahindra Showroom, Sector 2, Noida, UP and caused the injuries to injured Deepak Sharma?
OPP (2)Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP (3)Relief.
6. To substantiate his case petitioner Deepak Sharma examined himself as PW1 and examined another witness PW2 Dr.Abhishek Sharma.
No evidence has been led on behalf of respondents.

7. I have heard the submissions of Sh.Pradeep Kumar, ld. counsel for petitioner, Sh.H.V. Singh, ld.
counsel for R1 & R2 as MACT No.674/2017 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 3 MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:18:20 +0530 well as Sh.Ved Tripathi, ld. counsel for respondent no.3/
insurance company.

sentences.text: It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.

In the present case for proving rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1, petitioner/injured (PW1) in the accident has testified that on 30.09.2017 at about 2.00 p.m. he along with Durgesh Rathore was going on motorbike from Sector 45 to Sector 2 Noida and when they reached near Mahindra Showroom, Sector-2, Noida when a vehicle no.DL-4CAQ-9727 being driven at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came and hit their motorcycle.
As a result they both fell down on the road and received serious injuries.
PW1 stated that from the place of accident he was removed and admitted in Metro Hospital, Noida.

Though PW1 was duly cross examined on behalf of respondents, however nothing substantive came to disbelieve his testimony.
However during cross examination PW1 stated that he was driving the motorcycle at the time of accident and Durgesh was sitting as pillion rider and they were wearing helmets at the time of accident.
PW1 stated that the car hit him at the left side of his motorcycle.
Thus, evidence of PW1 is consistent, cogent and worthy of reliance for issue under consideration.
11. Beside the oral testimony of PW1, documents annexed with DAR also establish the rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle no.DL- 4CAQ-9727.
It is matter of record that respondent no.1 has been charge sheeted and is being prosecuted for the accident in question before concerned criminal court.

Site plan of the accident also indicate that motorcycle of the injured was hit by offending vehicle, this fact also gets corroboration from FIR wherein number of offending vehicle is mentioned, report u/s 173 Cr.P.C. etc.
As such when it is proved by preponderance of probabilities that accident occurred only because of rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle No.DL-4CAQ-9727.
Accordingly, issue stands decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount MACT No.674/2017 SHAILENDER Page 5 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:18:39 +0530 of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii)
loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.
13. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered MACT No.674/2017
Digitally
signed by SHAILENDER Page 6 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK
Date: 2024.05.07 16:18:46 +0530 as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of  prospects of marriage)
 (vi) Loss of expectation of life  (shortening of normal longevity).
MACT No.674/2017 Digitally signed  by SHAILENDER Page 7  SHAILENDER MALIK  MALIK Date: 2024.05.07  16:18:54 +0530

In routine personal injury cases,
compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
14.

Loss of earning during treatment:
16.
Petitioner/injured Deepak Sharma (PW1) in his deposition stated that at the time of accident he was doing private service and earning Rs.16,000/- per month.
During cross examination PW1 stated that he has not placed any document I support of his occupation and income as claimed by him.
There is no evidence on record to show what was the occupation or work of the petitioner and what was he earning at the time of accident.
Petitioner has placed on record his Aadhar card Ex.PW2/1 which shows that he is resident of Delhi.

In the absence of any evidence regarding occupation and income of petitioner, this Tribunal assesses notional income of petitioner at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker at the time of accident in Delhi i.e. Rs.13,584/- per month.
17. As per PW1 petitioner continued taking treatment since the date of accident and remained admitted in hospital from time to time.
Having considered the entire medical documents Ex.PW1/1 as well as the evidence of PW1, petitioner is entitled for loss of income for period of 12 months.
As such a sum of Rs.1,63,008/- (Rs.13,584 X 12 months) is granted as compensation to the petitioner under this head.

Loss of future earning due to disability :
18.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

sentences.text: Petitioner (PW1) in his deposition stated that he spent Rs.50,000/- on conveyance and Rs.50,000/- on special diet.
However during cross examination PW1 stated that he has not placed any document in support of his claim regarding expenses incurred on conveyance and special diet.

Though there is no document regarding claim of special diet and conveyance charges, however fact remains that as per medical documents produced on record petitioner suffered fracture of left side ribs, spleen injuries, fracture of left tibia and two fractures in his left leg.
Surgery of petitioner was also conducted due to accidental injuries and he remain hospitalized in Metro Hospital.
It has also come in the evidence of petitioner that he remained admitted in Metro Hospital on different occasions.

Thus, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that petitioner must have incurred expenses towards special diet for his well being during the period of treatment and also incurred expenses towards going to hospital.
Thus this Tribunal awards compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of special diet and Rs.20,000/- under the head of conveyance charges to the petitioner.

Attendant Charges:
20.
Since this Tribunal has already assessed compensation to the petitioner for a period of 12 months under the head of loss of earning during treatment.

Though no documentary evidence in this regard has been led by the MACT No.674/2017 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 10 MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:19:22 +0530 petitioner, but fact remains that he suffered grievous injuries on different parts of his body.

Keeping in view the medical documents placed on record, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner must have engaged the services of some attendant and he is required to be awarded compensation under this head for a period of 12 months.
Therefore petitioner in the opinion of this Tribunal is also entitled for attendant charges @ Rs.6,000/- per month which comes out to be Rs.72,000/- (Rs.6,000 X 12 months).

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings:
21.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No: 709/02, date of decision:
02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
22.

In this case, as per medical documents of the petitioner, he was found to have suffered fracture of left side ribs, spleen injuries, fracture of left tibia and two fractures in his left leg in his body.
It is matter of record that surgery was conducted for the accidental injuries.

The medical treatment record of MACT No.674/2017 Digitally signed by SHAILENDER Page 11 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:19:31 +0530 petitioner as placed on record further shows that he had been taking continuous treatment.

Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
Accordingly, Rs.1,50,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
Loss of Amenities:

23. It is evident on record that due to accidental injuries i.e. fracture of ribs, spleen injuries, fracture of left tibia and fractures in left leg, petitioner suffered a lot and it cannot be ignored that with the aforementioned medical problems, petitioner is bound to face difficulties throughout his life and will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
In view of this, the petitioner is granted a compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
14.
17. As per PW1 petitioner continued taking treatment since the date of accident and remained admitted in hospital from time to time.
Having considered the entire medical documents Ex.PW1/1 as well as the evidence of PW1, petitioner is entitled for loss of income for period of 12 months.
As such a sum of Rs.1,63,008/- (Rs.13,584 X 12 months) is granted as compensation to the petitioner under this head.
In the absence of any such disability on record, petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
Thus, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that petitioner must have incurred expenses towards special diet for his well being during the period of treatment and also incurred expenses towards going to hospital.
Thus this Tribunal awards compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of special diet and Rs.20,000/- under the head of conveyance charges to the petitioner.
Keeping in view the medical documents placed on record, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner must have engaged the services of some attendant and he is required to be awarded compensation under this head for a period of 12 months.
Therefore petitioner in the opinion of this Tribunal is also entitled for attendant charges @ Rs.6,000/- per month which comes out to be Rs.72,000/- (Rs.6,000 X 12 months).
Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
